title: L0182
description: A compiled L0182 survey: the set of ideas someone was asked to choose between, drawn from the survey's own data by the compiler, and — once something has answered — the response to it, being the ideas chosen in priority order plus one new idea that was not in the set.

survey.description: The set of ideas and the bounds a response must satisfy. None of it is written in the program: the compiler reads it from the survey the program names.

id.description: The survey being taken, as the program named it. Ties a response back to the survey it answers.

sessionId.description: One taking of the survey. Seeded from the item id, and what keeps a response with the version of the survey it answers. Absent when the program named no session.

instance.description: Which version of the survey was taken — the file its ideas came from, e.g. you-can-choose-7. A survey with several versions draws one of them per session; writing this as the id takes that version outright.

instructions.description: What the participant is asked to do, shown under the title and above the ideas. Always present: the compiler substitutes a generic line when the survey's data supplies none. The bounds line beneath it is derived from minChoices and maxChoices.

ideas.description: The set a response is chosen from, compiled in from the survey's own data. A program cannot write it.

minChoices.description: Fewest ideas a response may select. The survey's own, defaulting to 1. Enforced by the compiler, which is the only enforcement there is — nothing renders a survey interactively.

maxChoices.description: Most ideas a response may select. The survey's own; never more than the number of ideas, defaulting to 5, or one fewer than the set when the set is smaller, so a default never permits choosing every idea.

response.description: The answer to this survey. Absent until something answers. Written in code — by a person in the editor, or by an agent through update_item — so both clients produce the identical shape.

selection.description: The ids of the ideas chosen, in priority order. The order IS the ranking, first is most important. Empty when only a new idea was contributed. Source may name an idea by its id in quotes or by its position as a number; the compiler resolves positions, so compiled output is always ids.

idea.description: One new idea from whoever answered, which was not already in the set.

idea.title: Idea
idea.description: One idea in the set. The id is the originating service's own where the survey's data carried one, and positional (i0 upward) where it did not — a selection names ids, never text.
